governance.decisionForum: King’s Edge Portfolio Board, with the team’s organisational, workforce and professional-practice arrangements governed through the relevant Digital and IT forums.
governance.decisionScope: Material decisions about the team’s remit; the four funded core posts, their planning grades, individual multi-year costs, final grades, start dates, future pay-award implications and post-mobilisation recurrent implications; whether solution architecture is covered within the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer post or separately; the small protected Business Analysis and DevOps/platform allocations; the £90,000 Year One agentic software-development tooling allowance and its final commercial implementation; leadership and decision rights; demand intake and prioritisation; any material increase in Hub scope that would compete with the King’s Edge roadmap; product and delivery practices; interfaces with specialist Digital and IT functions; evidence-based decisions to expand beyond the four-post core; handover criteria; and enduring institutional ownership.
governance.businessAsUsualOwner: TBC – Digital and IT product development capability owner
governance.businessAsUsualOwnershipNote: The capability is expected to sit within Digital and IT. The current mobilisation assumption is a 4.0 FTE funded core across the full three-year period to June 2029: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, 1.0 FTE Product & Service Designer and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer. Each post is individually profiled rather than sitting beneath a global staffing envelope. In constant 2026 planning prices, the four-post core is approximately £203,000 in 2026/27 for the eight-month November-to-June mobilisation period, then approximately £304,000 in each of 2027/28 and 2028/29, or approximately £811,000 across the three years. Digital and IT / HR must validate final grades, appointment points, start dates and future pay awards. Mark Peace is Product Owner. The Product & Service Designer combines UX/UI, service design, prototyping and user research. Outside the funded core, the working assumption is deliberately lean: approximately 0.2 FTE protected Business Analysis during the main discovery period and approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, with up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the senior engineering post cannot carry that function. Product quality assurance sits with the QA Engineer; specialist security, privacy, accessibility, data, architecture assurance and service-management input is drawn from existing institutional functions when required rather than represented as standing fractional posts. A £90,000 Year One planning allowance for ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling remains in the baseline while Digital and IT validates the exact commercial structure and whether shared capacity can reduce the eventual cost. The current overall Year One cash baseline remains approximately £358,000. Any staffing above the four-post core in Years Two and Three should be justified from evidence, while continuation of the core beyond June 2029 is a separate business-as-usual decision rather than an automatic recurrent commitment. The enduring organisational home, recurrent staffing, professional leadership and relationship to the Digital Student Experience Hub product and platform ownership under 4.1.2 should be confirmed as the operating model is proven.
